shared_elements: frontal standing human figure carved in relief on a tall vertical monolith
elaborate headdress / headgear filling the upper zone
circular disc or medallion on the chest (pectoral ornament)
broad belt or apron-like element across the lower torso
curvilinear scroll and mask-like motifs filling the surface
arms held symmetrically at the sides of the body across the chest
justification: Both surfaces depict a single frontal human figure occupying the whole face of a tall vertical monolith, with a massive ornamental headdress above the head, arms held symmetrically across the chest, a round pectoral disc at the centre of the torso, and a belt/apron zone below — a fairly specific and repeated scheme of stacked costume elements rather than a generic standing figure. The main difference is density and legibility of detail: B's surface is packed with interlocking masks, scrolls and glyph-like panels rendered with fine, naturalistic modelling, while A shows a much sparser, bolder, more schematic set of motifs with the face barely indicated.
